  File: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: lines 66 and 333 (descope path for fix-check-defective)
  Problem: The descope path for fix-check-defective opens a revert PR against the base branch that removes the de-scoped part, then resumes the fix check. The fix check at line 66 re-checks the fix PR's diff, which the revert PR does not change. If the revert removes code in files the fix PR did not touch, the fix-check sees the same diff and reports FIX-DEFECTIVE again, consuming the descope choice without resolving the stop.
  Why it fails at runtime: The judge already recorded descope for the stop+fingerprint, so allowed choices on the re-escalation omit descope. The only remaining choices may be close, prematurely ending the project. Contrast with the budget path for the same stop, which opens a fix PR targeting the specific unresolved findings and then fix-checks that new PR.

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  File: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: line 333 (and line 66)
  Problem: A descope choice for escalation stop fix-check-defective resumes the stage that stopped (conformance 3/3 — fix check) against the original fix PR, whose diff the revert PR does not modify.
  Why it fails at runtime: When fix-check-defective escalates and the judge selects descope, stage descope ES-<n> merges a revert PR to remove the defective code from the base branch. Line 333 sets the next stage on merge to "the stage that stopped", which for fix-check-defective is conformance 3/3 — fix check. That stage runs verify-activation.md with --scope fix-check #<fix PR>. Since #<fix PR> points to the original merged fix PR whose diff on GitHub is immutable and still contains the defect, verify-activation.md re-audits the original PR diff and returns FIX-DEFECTIVE again. This immediately re-escalates to fix-check-defective with descope already recorded in the ledger, wasting the descope attempt and pushing the failure toward an unwanted close.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===

- workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  File: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md
  Line or code reference: Escalations section, descope bullet (line 333)
  Problem: The descope path for `fix-check-defective` resumes the fix check against the original fix PR. The descope PR does not change that PR's diff, so the fix check audits the same code and reports FIX-DEFECTIVE again.
  Why it fails at runtime: When `fix-check-defective` fires and the judge picks `descope`, a revert PR is opened and merged. The next stage is the fix check, which re-audits the original fix PR's diff (unchanged) and reports the same defect. The stop fires again with the same fingerprint (the evidence's `pr` stays the original fix PR). `descope` is already recorded, so `allowed_choices` returns only `close`. The project is forced to close even though `descope` was supposed to be a working alternative to `close`.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The PR description's "Files" table should list all subcommands of `escalation_ledger.py`. The implementation exposes four subcommands (`fingerprint`, `allowed`, `grants`, `record`); the PR description's table lists only three (`fingerprint`, `allowed`, `record`), omitting `grants` which was added in the round-9 fix.
  Expected change site: PR description's `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py (new)` row
  Evidence of absence: The PR description's "Files" table row for the ledger says "`fingerprint`, `allowed`, `record`. No API calls. Exit 1 on bad arguments; exit 2 on an unreadable log or a malformed `## Escalations` line". The `grants` subcommand is not mentioned. The round-9 commit (the last run) added `grants` to `escalation_ledger.py` and updated `implement-plan-claude.md`, `CLAUDE.md §28.G`, and `agents.md` to reference it, but the PR description was not updated to match.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The PR description states "The judge picks one choice from a fixed menu (`budget`, `descope`, or `close`), never the same choice twice for the same failure (`.claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py`; the fingerprint of a PR-scoped stop includes the PR number)". The implementation and CLAUDE.md §28.G have been corrected to say "never picks `budget` or `descope` twice" (since `close` is intentionally always available, even after being recorded), but the PR description still uses the original wording that implies `close` also cannot repeat.
  Expected change site: PR description's "What changes" section, the menu sentence
  Evidence of absence: The PR description's invariant statement contradicts the corrected wording in CLAUDE.md §28.G ("never picks `budget` or `descope` when that choice is already recorded for the same stop and fingerprint"; "`close` is always available, even when it was picked before") and the implementation (`allowed_choices` always includes `close`; `test_record_refuses_a_used_choice` explicitly asserts `close` can repeat). The test `test_claude_md_section_28g` pins the corrected wording in CLAUDE.md but does not cover the PR description.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
